correctness.rationale: Only \(b\) can reduce image size and each application reduces rank by at most one, so deficiency \(s\) needs at least \(s\) effective \(b\)'s. After an effective \(b\), state \(n-1\) is missing. A subsequent effective \(b\) requires at least two intervening \(a\)'s: zero leaves \(n-1\) absent, while one rotates the unique relevant gap so that applying \(b\) cannot reduce cardinality. Thus every such word has length at least \(s+2(s-1)=3s-2\). For the displayed witness, induction gives the exact missing set after each effective \(b\); the range \(s\le\lceil n/2\rceil\) ensures the odd missing states do not wrap into the two states needed for the next contraction. Independently, subset-BFS for all \(3\le n\le11\) and every admissible \(s\) reproduced \(3s-2\) in 34 cases; the package artifact checks through \(n=12\).

value.rationale: Intermediate rank collapse is a standard refinement of synchronization, and the Černý family is the canonical extremal family. Determining the exact early half of its deficiency profile, with a matching lower-bound mechanism and explicit optimal witnesses, is a natural structural result rather than a finite census. It also separates the cheapest initial contractions from the much slower final reset phase.
residual_risks: The later deficiency range remains open in this record.

final_claim: For the standard \(n\)-state Černý automaton \(C_n\), let \(\lambda_n(s)\) be the minimum word length whose image has size at most \(n-s\). For every \(n\ge3\) and \(1\le s\le\lceil n/2\rceil\), \[\lambda_n(s)=3s-2,\] attained by \(b(a^2b)^{s-1}\); after the \(j\)-th effective \(b\), the missing-state set is \(\{1,3,\ldots,2j-3,n-1\}\).
limitations: Only the early deficiency range \(s\le\lceil n/2\rceil\) is determined.
The result does not classify all shortest words, all reachable subsets, or the later deficiency/reset profile.
